children.name: text
children: Upon receipt of the Default Payment Notice, where the Contractor considers (acting reasonably) that the Default Payment Notice does not comply with the requirements of {b:clause 4.6.7}, the Contractor shall as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event not later than five (5) days after receipt of the Default Payment Notice, give written notice (including its reasons) to the Sub-Contractor and the Sub-Contractor shall re-issue the Default Payment Notice to take into account such reasons. children: The Sub-Contractor undertakes and warrants that it shall:

children: .1 comply with all applicable laws, regulations, codes and sanctions relating to anti-bribery and anti-corruption including but not limited to the Bribery Act 2010 (the "Relevant Requirements");

children.name: text

children.name: text
children: The parties agree that breach of this {b:clause 7.6} shall entitle the Contractor to terminate this sub-contract on written notice, and {b:clause 7.7} shall apply.

For the purposes of this {b:clause 7.6} a person associated with the Sub-Contractor includes but is not limited to any sub-sub-contractor of the Sub-Contractor.

children.name: text
children: In performing its obligations under this Sub-Contract, the Sub-Contractor shall and shall ensure that each of its sub-subcontractors and consultants shall comply with:
.1    all applicable laws, statutes, regulations and codes from time to time in force including but not limited to the Modern Slavery Act 2015; and

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor represents and warrants that:
.1    its responses to the Contractor's slavery and human trafficking due diligence questionnaire are complete and accurate; and
.2    neither the Sub-Contractor nor any of its officers, employees or other persons associated with it:
(a)    has been convicted of any offence involving slavery and human trafficking; and

(b)    to the best of its knowledge has been or is the subject of any investigation, inquiry or enforcement proceedings by any governmental, administrative or regulatory body regarding any offence or alleged offence of or in connection with slavery and human trafficking.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall implement due diligence procedures for its own suppliers, sub-subcontractors, consultants and other participants in its supply chains, to ensure that there is no slavery or human trafficking in its supply chains.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall notify the Contractor as soon as it becomes aware of:
.1    any breach, or potential breach, of the Anti-Slavery Policy; or
.2    any actual or suspected slavery or human trafficking in a supply chain which has a connection with the Sub-Contract.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall prepare and deliver to the Contractor no later than 31 December each year, an annual slavery and human trafficking report setting out the steps it has taken to ensure that slavery and human trafficking is not taking place in any of its supply chains or in any part of its business.

children.name: text
children: .1    maintain a complete set of records to trace the supply chain of all Site Materials; and

children.name: text

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall implement a system of training for its employees, suppliers, sub-sub-contractors and consultants to ensure compliance with the Anti-Slavery Policy.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall keep a record of all training offered and completed by its employees, suppliers, sub-sub-contractors and consultants to ensure compliance with the Anti-Slavery Policy and shall make a copy of the record available to the Contractor on request.

children.name: text
children: The Sub-Contractor shall indemnify the Contractor against any losses, liabilities, damages, costs (including but not limited to legal fees) and expenses incurred by, or awarded against, the Contractor as a result of any breach of Anti-Slavery Policy.

children.name: text

children.name: text

children.name: text
children: The decision of the Adjudicator or the Connected Dispute Adjudicator shall be binding on the parties until the dispute or Connected Dispute is finally determined by legal proceedings. Either party may, not later than sixty (60) Business Days after the decision of the Adjudicator or the Connected Dispute Adjudicator serve a notice of Dissatisfaction (the "Notice of Dissatisfaction") on the other party. The Notice of Dissatisfaction shall set out the matters in dispute and the reason(s) for dissatisfaction. Provided that such notice has been served in accordance with this sub-clause (and irrespective of which party served the notice) either party shall thereafter be entitled to commence legal proceedings in respect of the matter or matters in dispute.

children.name: text
